summary: All three items are still open and doable now as tests only (re-verified against the repo and the binary). (1) M-16: the backlog premise 'FlatCells builds 16 px heights only' is wrong in practice. Slope kind 1 gives ground = cellHeight*16 - (floor(y) mod 16) with no x term, in the DLL (AlundraCellsCollisionField.cs:382-391) AND in the binary (ComputeEntityGroundHeight 0x8003722C-0x80037264, re-disassembled), so a hero walking east over a boundary between flat 16 px cells and kind-1 cells sees an exact constant integer step whose size is set by its y (PosY = 104 + d + 0.5 gives a d px drop, 1 <= d <= 14; y = 107.5 gives exactly 3 px). No change to FlatCells or to AlundraJumpTestSupport.cs (D5b territory) is needed. The binary rule at 0x80037848 snaps a descent of at most 0x30000 (3 px inclusive) when Gravity is set, ForceZ == 0 and the entity has a non-zero XY step (re-disassembled: 0x800377A0-0x800377A8 and 0x80037834-0x80037888). Today's UH-7b (hero hand-placed 3 px up while standing still) exercises the ENGINE's 4 px ground snap in a case the binary rule does not cover (zero XY step exits at 0x80037DC0). The rewrite walks east over a real 3 px step (UH-7's geometry) and pins no air state, ForceX 159744 each tick, PosZ 1048576 then 851968. (2) M-17: UH-17 only asserts NotEmpty(riding) and onFlush > 0. From the binary rider window (0x80036564-0x800365D4, re-disassembled; strict compares; hero width 21 px, object width 24 px) and the walk x(head of tick t) = 165 + 2.4375*(t-1), the riding ticks are predicted 8..26 and the HeroAirborne ticks 17..26 (re-derived independently from the DLL code and the engine corner rule: same result). They are pinned with Assert.Equal on the lists. X-window mutations (EntitySupport.cs:333 and :338) and the carrier-force copy removal (AlundraScriptedMotion.cs:303-306) turn the new pins red while every existing UH-17 assertion stays green; the Y-window mutation named in the triage does NOT discriminate here, and the triage's 'F3 flag' mutation is already red under the existing assertions. (3) SJ-12: both ternary branches are the same expression; Assert.True(hero.ForceZ == 0, ...) is behaviour-neutral. M-19's other parts are not open (renames done by E19.m6, M-19c closed without change, untested branches closed with written reasons). All expected values are DERIVED by reading (no dotnet in this task): the first run must measure them, and any divergence is a stop, not a re-pin.

facts.claim: BINARY: the kind-1 branch of ComputeEntityGroundHeight (0x800370C4) has no x term either: height = ((tileHeight-1)<<4) + 0x10 - (ys[i] mod 16), taken when (slopesHit & 6) == 0; otherwise +0x10 (the 'slopesHit' bump). slopesHit gets bit 1 from a kind-1 corner, so the bump only fires after a kind-2 or kind-3 corner. The class-doc deviation about the +16 bump (AlundraCellsCollisionField.cs:135-141) therefore does not apply to a footprint of kind-0 and kind-1 cells: the terrain of the proposed fixture is binary-faithful, not only DLL-faithful. facts.claim: The exported hero controller has ground_snap_distance 4.0 and step_height 3.0 (tests load the real export). The engine accepts a field ground when groundHeight >= footUpAfterStep - GroundSnapDistance (inclusive: exactly 4 px is accepted) and <= probe origin; the comparison is at CharacterControllerComponent.cs:1535. StepHeight enters the DESCENT only through the upper bound 'origin = footUpBeforeStep + max(StepHeight, verticalDelta)' (:1527) and the horizontal block test (:1340-1356, blocks only ground ABOVE foot + StepHeight), so cutting StepHeight cannot make a descent fall. While grounded the engine zeroes downward velocity (ApplyVerticalVelocity :807-816) so verticalDelta is 0 on the walking frame and the classification is clean: a 3 px drop is accepted, a 5 px drop is rejected.

facts.claim: Binary rule for a small descent: in ComputeXYPosition, after the candidate XY position, ModdedPosZ (+0x1E0 = PosZ+ModZ) and the terrain T' at the new position (jal 0x800370C4) are computed, if Gravity (+0x6C & 0x100) is set and ForceZ (+0xB8) == 0, with d = T' - ModdedPosZ - 1: snap when d >= 0 and d < 0x30000, or d < 0 and |d| < 0x30003; then PosZ(+0x11C) = T'+1, undone if an entity occupies the box (0x80036F34). At rest the binary's ModdedPosZ = T_old + 1, so a descent of k gives d = -k-2 and the snap holds iff k <= 0x30000: exactly 3 px is INSIDE, 3 px + 1 unit is outside.

production_change: None. Tests only: no Alundra/ file, no engine or analyser submodule file, no converter, no export, no cmp change, no trace change.
chain_impact: None. The story chain, exports and the six hero/intro traces are untouched. Alundra.Tests count grows by 1 (the Fact becomes a Theory of 2 cases) or 2 (with the optional control). Value for the player: none (test fidelity only), as the triage says.
risks: All expected values in this report are derived from code and disassembly, not measured (no dotnet allowed here). The first execution must measure them; per the repo convention a measured value that differs from the written one is a stop to analyse, not a re-pin. The riding upper bound has a 0.0625 px margin at tick 26 (225.9375 vs 226) and depends on every tick adding exactly 159744 px/65536; the evidence is no obstacle probe, a Kinetic ghost object and UH-7's exact PosX, so confirm it in the first dump.

The 3 px step relies on the engine's and the DLL's footprint corners agreeing on y (verified by reading: same 21x15 box, BitDecrement far edge) and on the engine sampling only 4 corners (verified). A hero y on an integer boundary could shift a corner by a row; use the fractional y values given.
Pinning the 4 px case would encode the O-E19-40 deviation (engine snaps 4 px, binary falls); a future engine plan that resolves ground per tick would turn it red by design. Pin only 3 px and 5 px.

The airborne list of UH-17 (17..26) pins DLL design (F3 state at rest on a flush top), not a binary field. D5b option (A) or a change to F3 could move it; the riding list is binary-derived and robust. If D5b resumes first, update the airborne pin in the same commit; to be D5b-insensitive, pin only the riding list and the first and last airborne ticks.

Mutation runs on engine or Alundra/ files must restore the exact bytes; the engine submodule has an unrelated modified file (CasaEngine.Launcher/Program.cs), so never use a blanket checkout there. Another process is building: do not run mutations or dotnet concurrently with it.

Parallel-edit risk with D5b: AlundraHeroObjectTopsTests.cs is D5b's file for UH-16 and others; keep the diff to UH-17 and line 373 so a later D5b merge stays trivial. AlundraJumpTestSupport.cs is not needed and should stay untouched.
